Emma — thanks, we received the package. Looping in our privacy counsel (Marissa) and contracts lead (Kim) so we can run the redlines and respond with an internal consolidated view. Quick, high-level answers so you have immediate context: 

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood's standard execution uses the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) for transfers from the EEA/UK, plus our DPA includes an EU/UK Addendum. Where an adequacy decision applies for a given country we will note it but we do not rely on adequacy as the primary contractual safeguard in the DPA. Marissa/Legal will confirm the final language.

- Subprocessors: The most common subprocessors are cloud compute (AWS, GCP), observability (Datadog), and a managed vector-store partner for embeddings. We will produce an Exhibit S that maps each subprocessor to processing purposes (production inference vs telemetry/analytics).

- Logging: We do not share customer prompt/response content with third-party logging vendors. Observability telemetry is redacted or aggregated; we will include a definitive statement in the Exhibit S and the evidence pack.

We can do a 30-minute review call tomorrow or Wednesday. Proposed slots: 2026-11-22 10:00–10:30 PT or 2026-11-23 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?

Next steps: Marissa will send counsel comments in-thread; Kim will coordinate the consolidated redline for DocuSign routing. We aim to return a consolidated vendor redline + evidence bundle within 48 business hours after your call.

Thanks — V

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Emma Jones <emma.jones@lucenthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:28:00Z
Subject: Privacy counsel comments — LucentHealth Round 1 redlines

Hi team / Emma,

I reviewed LucentHealth's Round 1 redlines and Exhibit S. Below are counsel-level comments and requests for clarification/evidence. I highlight suggested language changes where we anticipate negotiation friction.

1) Transfer mechanism (SCCs / addenda)
- Suggest we confirm explicit citation to the 2021 SCCs (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/...) in the DPA, plus include a short EU Addendum that mirrors the SCCs' technical/organizational measures references. This is our standard.
- If Lucent prefers an alternative (e.g., DPF or contractual alone), ask them to identify the clauses they want to change. We will not accept a solution that lacks SCCs as the base mechanism for EEA transfers.

2) Subprocessor categorization in Exhibit S
- Request: Exhibit S must map subprocessor -> processing purpose ("production inference", "embeddings/vector-store", "telemetry/metrics", "support/ops"). This avoids ambiguity in the DPA's access clauses.
- Notice period: we generally accept a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors. For high-risk subprocessors (defined below) propose a shorter review window (15 days) and an explicit right to object.

3) Definition of "high-risk"
- Proposed carve: any subprocessor with access to unredacted customer content or that performs model training on customer data. Examples: managed vector-store if it stores raw prompts/responses; any partner that does training or long-term retention of content.

4) Logging & telemetry
- We need to confirm that 3rd-party logging/observability vendors receive only metadata/aggregated telemetry. If any raw content is temporarily available (e.g., for debugging), it must be limited, timeboxed, and governed by a documented process. Provide specifics and a statement for Exhibit S.

5) Security & encryption
- Confirm encryption at rest and in transit, and availability of customer-managed KMS/HSM for enterprise customers. If available, we should offer the option in Exhibit S for customers who require key control.

6) Evidence pack (please prepare)
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent)
- Data flow diagram showing cross-border flows for Lucent-specific integration
- Subprocessor inventory CSV with region, purpose, and whether they see content
- SCCs adoption note (short doc explaining how we implement SCC clauses operationally)

7) Suggested clause edits (high level)
- Replace broad "standard transfer mechanisms" language with explicit SCC adoption language and the process for addressing future regulatory changes.
- Add an explicit commitment that third-party support vendors will not access customer prompt/response content except where required for troubleshooting with customer authorization.

I'll prepare a marked-up DPA (consolidated counsel view) for review after the call. Attaching a short SCCs-adoption-note and a draft subprocessor matrix template for internal use.

Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: SCCs-adoption-note.pdf (pdf), Subprocessor_matrix_draft.csv (csv)

- Exhibit S v2 (attached) narrows the subprocessor list and marks which vendors are "production inference" vs "analytics/telemetry". Please review and confirm.
- Transfer mechanism: Lucent is fine proceeding with the 2021 SCCs + EU Addendum; we had raised the question only to confirm explicit language.
- Notice period: Lucent typically requests 15-day notice for new "high-risk" subprocessors. We're willing to accept 30 days for lower-risk vendors. Our ask: include a short definition of "high-risk" in Exhibit S (we propose the same definition Marissa suggested).
- Logging: we require an explicit statement that logging/observability vendors do not have access to customer prompt/response content and that any temporary access for debugging must be documented and approved by Lucent.

Attached: Exhibit_S_v2.pdf (updated subprocessor mapping)
